title: The Normal-Subgroup Three Subgroups Lemma (commutator_le_of_rotate)
content: The headline result: for N normal, ⁅⁅H,K⁆,L⁆ ≤ N and ⁅⁅K,L⁆,H⁆ ≤ N imply ⁅⁅L,H⁆,K⁆ ≤ N. The proof is a quotient transport. First rewrite each `_ ≤ N` as `_ ≤ (QuotientGroup.mk' N).ker` using QuotientGroup.ker_mk' (the kernel of the canonical projection is exactly N), then as `(QuotientGroup.mk' N).map _ = ⊥` using Subgroup.map_eq_bot_iff. The simp lemma Subgroup.map_commutator distributes the projection through both nested brackets, turning each hypothesis and the goal into a statement about the images ⁅⁅map f H, map f K⁆, map f L⁆ in G ⧸ N. Mathlib's bottom-case lemma Subgroup.commutator_commutator_eq_bot_of_rotate then closes the goal verbatim in the quotient group.
mathContext: $\lbrack\lbrack H,K\rbrack,L\rbrack \le N \;\wedge\; \lbrack\lbrack K,L\rbrack,H\rbrack \le N \;\Rightarrow\; \lbrack\lbrack L,H\rbrack,K\rbrack \le N$, for $N \trianglelefteq G$.
prerequisites: QuotientGroup.mk' N and QuotientGroup.ker_mk' (kernel of the projection equals N)
Subgroup.map_eq_bot_iff (X.map f = ⊥ ⟺ X ≤ f.ker) and Subgroup.map_commutator (map distributes over the bracket)
significance: The classical ≤ N form of the three subgroups lemma, which Mathlib lacks. This is the version used inductively to prove ⁅γᵢ,γⱼ⁆ ≤ γ₍ᵢ₊ⱼ₎ for the lower central series; obtaining it from the absolute case by a quotient argument is the original content of the entry.

title: Full Cyclic Symmetry (commutator_le_of_rotate₂, commutator_le_of_rotate₃)
content: The statement is invariant under the cyclic relabelling (H,K,L) ↦ (K,L,H), so the single lemma supplies all three implications among ⁅⁅H,K⁆,L⁆, ⁅⁅K,L⁆,H⁆, ⁅⁅L,H⁆,K⁆: any two lying in N force the third. commutator_le_of_rotate₂ derives ⁅⁅H,K⁆,L⁆ ≤ N from the other two, and commutator_le_of_rotate₃ derives ⁅⁅K,L⁆,H⁆ ≤ N; each is the main lemma with arguments permuted.
mathContext: Any two of $\lbrack\lbrack H,K\rbrack,L\rbrack, \lbrack\lbrack K,L\rbrack,H\rbrack, \lbrack\lbrack L,H\rbrack,K\rbrack$ contained in $N$ force the third.
prerequisites: The cyclic invariance of the iterated-commutator triple
significance: Exposes the lemma's full symmetry so that it can be applied in whichever of the three orientations a downstream proof needs, without re-deriving the quotient argument.

title: Inner-Commutator-First Formulation (commutator_le_of_rotate_symm)
content: The textbook bracket notation usually writes the iterated commutator with the inner bracket first, ⁅H,⁅K,L⁆⁆. Since the commutator of subgroups is symmetric (Subgroup.commutator_comm : ⁅A,B⁆ = ⁅B,A⁆), rewriting each commutator with commutator_comm turns the symmetric-notation statement into the main lemma: from ⁅L,⁅H,K⁆⁆ ≤ N and ⁅H,⁅K,L⁆⁆ ≤ N conclude ⁅K,⁅L,H⁆⁆ ≤ N.
mathContext: $\lbrack L,\lbrack H,K\rbrack\rbrack \le N \;\wedge\; \lbrack H,\lbrack K,L\rbrack\rbrack \le N \;\Rightarrow\; \lbrack K,\lbrack L,H\rbrack\rbrack \le N$.
prerequisites: Subgroup.commutator_comm (symmetry of the bracket on subgroups)
significance: Matches the form of the lemma found in standard group theory texts, making the result directly usable regardless of the bracket-nesting convention a reader or downstream proof adopts.

title: Bottom Case and Centralizing Corollary (commutator_eq_bot_of_rotate, commutator_commutator_le_of_both)
content: commutator_eq_bot_of_rotate specialises N = ⊥: since ≤ ⊥ collapses to = ⊥ (le_bot_iff), the normal-form lemma reproduces Mathlib's Subgroup.commutator_commutator_eq_bot_of_rotate exactly, confirming the generalization is faithful. commutator_commutator_le_of_both is the standard corollary: if H commutes with both K and L modulo the normal N (i.e. ⁅H,K⁆ ≤ N and ⁅H,L⁆ ≤ N), then H commutes with ⁅K,L⁆ modulo N. The proof forces two of the three iterated commutators into N — ⁅⁅H,K⁆,L⁆ ≤ ⁅N,L⁆ ≤ N and ⁅⁅L,H⁆,K⁆ ≤ ⁅N,K⁆ ≤ N, using Subgroup.commutator_mono and Subgroup.commutator_le_left (⁅N,·⁆ ≤ N for normal N) — and invokes the lemma to obtain the third, ⁅⁅K,L⁆,H⁆ = ⁅H,⁅K,L⁆⁆ ≤ N.
mathContext: $N=\bot$ recovers Mathlib's lemma; and $\lbrack H,K\rbrack \le N \wedge \lbrack H,L\rbrack \le N \Rightarrow \lbrack H,\lbrack K,L\rbrack\rbrack \le N$.
prerequisites: Subgroup.commutator_mono (monotonicity of the bracket) and Subgroup.commutator_le_left (⁅N,K⁆ ≤ N for normal N)
Subgroup.commutator_comm and the cyclic lemma commutator_le_of_rotate₃
significance: Demonstrates the generalization recovers the known result, and exhibits its typical use: a normal subgroup that absorbs two pairwise commutators also absorbs the commutator with the derived bracket — the propagation step underlying nilpotency arguments.
